chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him saying: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah conferred a favor upon the sick and travelers of His nation by reducing [the obligation] and by breaking the fast. Does one of you like that when he gives a charity, it is returned to him?'

key_terms.بالتقصير: By reducing [the number of days to fast]
key_terms.تَصَدَّقَ: Conferred a favor / granted a concession

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of Allah 'conceding a favor' to the sick and travelers regarding fasting?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) characterizes the divine concessions for the sick and travelers—specifically the permission to break the fast or shorten prayers—as an act of *tasadduq* (voluntary charity) by Allah, emphasizing the generosity of the Divine. The rhetorical question underscores that this grace is a unilateral favor, not a transaction requiring equivalent repayment, thereby highlighting the ease (*rukhas*) Allah has granted to alleviate hardship. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that these concessions are distinct from the obligatory make-up (*qada*) or expiation (*kaffarah*), serving primarily as a mercy rather than a burden.
